title: Brothers who played the fife in New Orleans
summary: Barnes says his brother Mealy led the family in playing the fife, which he took up at six. Another older brother was accidentally shot trying to stop a fight.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I didn't think so, you know, because I know you and your brother are both musicians, and I was wondering, did you have other brothers and sisters who were musicians?

Yes, I had one, but he didn't take up an instrument, but he used to play a fife just like I did. Oh really? Yeah. Just the same as my oldest brother, Mealy. He's the ringleader of it. He played the fife. And during those times the fife was very popular around New Orleans. If you don't know what a fife is, it's just a little instrument with six holes in it. Something you would play like a piccolo. It didn't have keys on the side, just three little holes, but you would be surprised the music that we could get out of that. It was very popular in New Orleans. I think besides my brother Sidney, Bessier, all of them played, played those little fife. And I actually started playing them when I was six years old.
Oh that's young. Well how old was your other brother? Was he older than you?
They were both older than me.
Oh, I never knew you had another brother.

I did. He was accidentally killed. Accidentally shot. Really? Yeah. All through it. He was trying to stop a fight and he accidentally got shot. Really? Oh that's sad. It was sad. But he was three years old than I.
